title: Permission synthesizer and request gating bridge for RBAC v2 across API/runtime/console
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design and implement a Permission Synthesizer service plus a lightweight Request Gating Bridge that jointly provide RBAC v2 decision semantics for API, runtime, and Console. The synthesizer will transform high-level role/group/permission manifests and SAML attribute mappings into a compact, precompiled decision graph optimized for low-latency evaluation and partial materialization in the runtime. The gating bridge is a small, sidecarless middleware that applies the compiled graph to each incoming request, enriches audit events with SAML/SSO attributes, and emits structured explainability logs for post-hoc inspection. Goals: deterministic <5ms median decision latency at p99 scaling to 10k req/s per region, end-to-end auditable decisions, admin emergency bypass/allowlist, and controlled rollout via canary feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Synthesizer accepts canonical role + permission + attribute mapping manifests and produces a compact decision graph artifact (JSON) with a verifiable checksum.
Gating Bridge evaluates compiled artifacts and returns allow/deny decisions via HTTP headers with <5ms median latency on benchmark workloads.
Audit pipeline receives enriched event payloads containing SAML groups, mapped entitlements, decision_id, and explainability trace.
Console admin flows use the same synthesized artifact and show decision explanations in the UI when verbose mode is enabled.
Canary rollout supports per-tenant evaluation toggles and automatic rollback on regression alerts (quality or latency).
Security review completed and KMS-integrated signing of synthesized artifacts in place.
tasks: Spec: permission synthesizer input language and compact decision graph format
Prototype: in-memory synthesizer and evaluator (Go) with unit tests
Middleware: implement Request Gating Bridge as Envoy filter + native library fallback
SSO/SAML: attribute mapper to normalize SAML groups to internal entitlements
Audit: extend audit schema with decision_id, explainability, saml_group_snapshot
Rollout plan: canary toggles, observability dashboards, regression queries
Security: artifact signing and CSR for key rotation, submit SR review ticket

notes: Trade-offs considered: eager full-policy evaluation vs incremental short-circuiting (we defaulted to short-circuiting with deterministic fallback to full evaluation for explainability). Cache eviction strategy uses strong-consistency TTL tied to role-modification events; plan includes an async invalidation bus. Operator emergency allowlist will be gated by audit-only opt-in and require two-person approval for full bypass.
